findings.blocking_reason: This is a behavioral regression: removing the 10-second clock skew tolerance from isActive() will cause previously-valid tokens to be rejected in production due to minor clock skew, breaking authentication flows.
findings.body: The no-arg `isActive()` method changed from `isActive(10)` to `isActive(0)`, removing the default 10-second clock skew tolerance for JWT validation. The previous code explicitly referenced the FAPI 2.0 specification requirement of 10 seconds tolerance. With 0 seconds tolerance, any token whose `exp` or `nbf` falls even 1 millisecond before the verifier's clock will be rejected as inactive. This can cause valid tokens to be rejected in production due to minor clock skew between distributed servers, breaking authentication flows. If this is an intentional tightening, callers must be updated to pass an explicit skew value. If unintentional, it is a security/availability regression.
findings.title: Removed default clock skew tolerance in isActive() (10s → 0s)

findings.blocking_reason: Removing the ECDSA verification branch is a regression that breaks token verification for all ES256/ES384/ES512 deployments that previously worked.
findings.body: The `case ECDSA:` block in `verify()` — which called `ECDSAProvider.verify(jws, publicKey)` — was deleted entirely, along with the `ECDSAProvider` import. The switch now only handles RSA and HMAC. The `AlgorithmType.ECDSA` enum value still exists, so ECDSA-signed tokens (ES256/ES384/ES512) will either fall through to the `null == algorithmType` branch (throwing "Unknown or unsupported token algorithm") or silently skip verification. Additionally, `ECDSAProvider.java` was deleted from the codebase. If ECDSA verification was not relocated to another verification path, this is a critical regression: ES256/ES384/ES512 tokens can no longer be verified, breaking any deployment using EC keys for token signing.
findings.evidence: Removed: `case ECDSA:\n    return ECDSAProvider.verify(jws, publicKey);` and `import org.keycloak.jose.jws.crypto.ECDSAProvider;`. File `core/src/main/java/org/keycloak/jose/jws/crypto/ECDSAProvider.java` was deleted (83 lines).
findings.title: Removed ECDSA verification branch from TokenVerifier.verify()

findings.blocking_reason: Removing otherClaims support is a regression that silently drops custom JWS header parameters previously handled during serialization/deserialization, breaking public API behavior that real extensions and SPIs depend on.
findings.body: The `otherClaims` field and its `@JsonAnyGetter`/`@JsonAnySetter` annotations were removed from `JWSHeader`. This means any custom or non-standard JWS header claims (e.g., `kid` aliases, custom header parameters defined in RFC 7515 §4.1 or extension specs) will be silently dropped during serialization and unavailable during deserialization. This is a breaking change for any extension, SPI, or third-party integration that relies on custom JWS header parameters. It also violates the permissive parsing principle of JWS (RFC 7515 allows header parameters not in the fixed set).
findings.evidence: Removed: `protected Map<String, Object> otherClaims = new HashMap<>();`, `@JsonAnyGetter public Map<String, Object> getOtherClaims()`, `@JsonAnySetter public void setOtherClaims(...)`. Switched from `JsonSerialization` to static `ObjectMapper` with `NON_NULL` inclusion.
findings.title: Removed otherClaims map and @JsonAnyGetter/@JsonAnySetter from JWSHeader

findings.blocking_reason: The PR on a stale branch silently reverts a previously merged behavior change (clock skew compliance) and removes helper methods, constituting a regression of working behavior.
findings.body: The PR is on a stale branch (2025-07-18) and unintentionally reverts commit `e278a2f6fd` (2026-01-22) which changed `isActive()` from `isActive(0)` to `isActive(10)` for FAPI 2.0 compliance. The FAPI 2.0 Javadoc and several helper methods (`issuedNowWithTTL`, `equals`, `hashCode`, `toString`) are also removed. The PR is about passkeys, not clock skew — this is collateral. **Fix: rebase onto current main.**
findings.title: Silent revert of FAPI 2.0 clock skew compliance

findings.blocking_reason: Missing test assertions for a form element is a test coverage gap, not a build/test breakage or production regression.
findings.body:
### Gap

The PR adds 5 positive re-auth Arquillian tests across three test classes, and **all 5 assert only `//form[@id='webauth']`** is present. **None assert `//form[@id='authn_select']`** — the form that carries the hidden `authn_use_chk` credentialId inputs used by the conditional UI autofill.

### Why it matters

I traced the full render path:

1. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` → `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError()` (sets `USERNAME_HIDDEN`, `REGISTRATION_DISABLED`) → `fillContextForm(context)`
2. `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` builds a `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` for the user and, **if the user has registered passkeys**, sets `form.setAttribute("authenticators", authenticators)` (the `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` constant).
3. `passkeys.ftl` renders `<form id="authn_select">` **only when `authenticators??`** — i.e. only for users with passkeys.

So during re-auth of a user **with** passkeys, the `authn_select` form **is** rendered with one `<input type="hidden" name="authn_use_chk" value="${authenticator.credentialId}">` per registered credential. This form feeds the browser's passkey autofill with the available credential IDs — functionally distinct from the `webauth` form, which collects the assertion response. For users **without** passkeys, the bean list is empty → early return → attribute never set → form not rendered.

The two forms serve different roles in the conditional-UI contract, and only one is tested.

### Recommended test additions

In the positive re-auth tests (e.g. `PasskeysPasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`, `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`), add alongside the existing `webauth` assertion:

And in the negative re-auth test (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`), assert the form is **absent**:

This pins the theme contract for both branches of `fillContextForm`'s empty-list guard and protects against regressions where the `authenticators` attribute is accidentally dropped from the re-auth error path.
findings.evidence: The PR adds 5 positive re-auth Arquillian tests across three test classes, and all 5 assert only `//form[@id='webauth']` is present. None assert `//form[@id='authn_select']`
findings.title: Missing `authn_select` form assertion during re-auth

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely demonstrate that any real caller is broken; it only speculates that callers 'must be audited' without showing evidence of a compile failure or broken contract in production.
findings.body: The `x5c` field in `JWSBuilder` changed from `List<String>` (base64-encoded strings per RFC 7515) to `List<X509Certificate>`. Base64 encoding now happens at JSON build time. This is a breaking API change: any code calling `x5c(List<String>)` will fail to compile, and any code introspecting the builder's x5c value will see a different type. While the runtime serialization may be correct, the compile-time contract has changed. All callers must be audited.
findings.evidence: Field type changed: `List<String> x5c` → `List<X509Certificate> x5c`. Encoding moved from setter to JSON build block.
findings.title: x5c field type changed from List<String> to List<X509Certificate>

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely demonstrate that any real caller depends on the removed setters; the impact is speculative.
findings.body: All setter methods were removed from `JWSHeader`: `setAlgorithm`, `setType`, `setContentType`, `setKeyId`, `setKey`, `setX5c`. The `addX5c(String)` and `addX5c(Certificate)` helper methods were also removed. The class is now effectively immutable (constructed only via constructor). While immutability is a positive design direction, this is a breaking change for any code that mutates a JWSHeader after construction (e.g., copying and modifying headers).
findings.title: JWSHeader made immutable — all setters and addX5c methods removed

findings.blocking_reason: Removing equals(), hashCode(), and toString() is a regression of existing behavior that could break token usage in collections and logging output.
findings.body: The `equals()`, `hashCode()`, and `toString()` methods were removed from `JsonWebToken`. This breaks: (1) usage of tokens in collections (HashMap, HashSet) since identity comparison replaces value comparison; (2) debugging and logging output since `toString()` now produces the default `ClassName@hash`. Any code relying on value-based equality of token representations will behave differently.
findings.title: Removed equals(), hashCode(), and toString() from JsonWebToken

findings.blocking_reason: The finding speculates with 'likely referenced' and does not concretely demonstrate that real callers depend on the removed field, constant, or constructor signature.
findings.body: The `originalAudience` field, `ORIGINAL_AUD` constant, and `getOriginalAudience()` method were removed from `RefreshToken`. The constructor signature also changed (removed `provider` parameter). Any code that reads the original audience from a refresh token (e.g., for audience-based routing or validation) will break. The `ORIGINAL_AUD` constant was likely referenced by other modules for claim name lookups.
findings.title: Removed originalAudience field and ORIGINAL_AUD constant from RefreshToken

findings.blocking_reason: Removing a public claim from AccessToken breaks the API/schema contract for any OIDC client relying on authorization_details, with no migration path.
findings.body: The `authorizationDetails` field (mapped to `@JsonProperty(OAuth2Constants.AUTHORIZATION_DETAILS)`), its getter and setter were removed from `AccessToken`. This claim is defined in RFC 9396 (OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata) for rich authorization requests. Any OIDC client or relying party that reads `authorization_details` from access tokens will no longer receive this data. This is a breaking change for deployments using RFC 9396.
findings.evidence: Removed: `@JsonProperty(OAuth2Constants.AUTHORIZATION_DETAILS) protected List<AuthorizationDetails> authorizationDetails;` and associated accessors.
findings.title: Removed authorization_details claim from AccessToken

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a possible API break for hypothetical custom Scope implementations but does not concretely demonstrate real callers that currently depend on AbstractScope or Scope.root().
findings.body: The `AbstractScope` abstract class was removed — `SystemPropertiesScope` now directly implements `Scope`. The `Scope.root()` static method was also removed. Any custom `Scope` implementations that extended `AbstractScope` will fail to compile, and any code calling `Scope.root()` to obtain the root scope will break. This affects SPI providers and test fixtures that interact with Keycloak's configuration system.
findings.title: Removed AbstractScope class and Scope.root() method

findings.blocking_reason: The finding only speculates about potential downstream NPEs without concretely demonstrating a reachable production code path that breaks; the behavioral change for OKP keys is described as a 'potential' regression, not a demonstrated one.
findings.body: The `getAlgorithmOrDefault()` method was rewritten to use a static `DEFAULT_ALGORITHM_BY_TYPE` map that only contains `RSA → RS256`. EC and OKP key types without an explicit algorithm will now return `null` instead of a sensible default (previously ES256/EdDSA). Any code that calls `getAlgorithmOrDefault()` on an EC or OKP `KeyWrapper` without a pre-set algorithm will get `null`, potentially causing NPEs or signing/verification failures downstream. Note: the old code had a latent bug (EC case fell through to RSA case due to missing `break`), so the new code is cleaner, but the behavioral change for OKP keys is a potential regression.
findings.evidence: Old: switch with cases for RSA, EC (fell through to RSA), OKP. New: `DEFAULT_ALGORITHM_BY_TYPE` map with only RSA entry.
findings.title: getAlgorithmOrDefault() no longer returns defaults for EC or OKP key types

findings.blocking_reason: The finding speculates about possible callers but does not concretely demonstrate any existing code uses getKeyType() or the ECDSA constant; if it did, the build would already fail.
findings.body: The `getKeyType(String keyAlgorithm)` method and `ECDSA` constant were removed from `JavaAlgorithm`. Any code using `getKeyType()` to map algorithm names to key types (RSA/EC/OKP) will fail to compile. This may affect key generation or import code that infers key type from algorithm name.
findings.title: Removed JavaAlgorithm.getKeyType() and ECDSA constant

findings.blocking_reason: The finding does not concretely demonstrate that real callers depend on the removed method or protected field; breakage of hypothetical custom subclasses is speculative, not a proven public API regression.
findings.body: The `getCertificateChain()` method was removed from `AsymmetricSignatureSignerContext`, and the `key` field was changed from `protected` to `private`. Any subclass that accessed the `key` field directly or overrode/used `getCertificateChain()` will break. This affects custom signature signer context implementations.
findings.title: Removed getCertificateChain() and changed key field visibility to private

findings.blocking_reason: Missing edge-case test coverage is explicitly non-blocking per the bar.
findings.body: `isExpired()` uses strict `>`, so a token expiring exactly now is still active. No test covers this boundary. The review question explicitly asked about this.
findings.title: Missing boundary test for `exp == currentTime`

findings.blocking_reason: This is an incomplete rollout of a new feature (passkey UI on the password page) in the base theme, not a regression or breakage — the password form still works and no existing behavior is lost.
findings.body:
**`base/login/login-password.ftl`** does NOT import `passkeys.ftl` nor call `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />`, while `keycloak.v2/login/login-password.ftl` (line 4 and line 18) does. This creates an asymmetry with `base/login/login.ftl` (line 2, line 83) and `base/login/login-username.ftl` (line 2, line 60), which both import passkeys and call the macro.

This PR enables passkeys during re-authentication (`prompt=login`). The re-auth password page is rendered by `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` → `challenge()` → `forms.createLoginUsernamePassword()` → `login-password.ftl` (see `Templates.java` line 34: `LOGIN_PASSWORD → "login-password.ftl"`).

The backend correctly sets `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI=true` and fills all WebAuthn model data (`challenge`, `rpId`, `userVerification`, `createTimeout`, `authenticators`) via `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` in `UsernamePasswordForm` line 115-117 and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` line 51-55. **However, in the `base` theme, none of this data is ever rendered** because `login-password.ftl` never calls `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />`.

The `passkeys.ftl` macro renders:
1. A `webauth` form with hidden inputs: `clientDataJSON`, `authenticatorData`, `signature`, `credentialId`, `userHandle`, `error` — needed to submit WebAuthn assertion data
2. An `authn_select` form with `authn_use_chk` hidden inputs for each authenticator's `credentialId` — needed for authenticator selection
3. The `authenticateWebAuthnButton` link and the JS module that initializes conditional passkey authentication

**Impact**: Any custom theme that extends `base` (or the legacy `keycloak` theme which also falls back to `base`) and does not override `login-password.ftl` will silently lose passkey conditional UI on the password page. During re-auth with `prompt=login`, users on such themes cannot use passkeys — no passkey button appears, no hidden form fields exist to receive WebAuthn assertion data, and no error or warning is shown. The password form itself still works, so the degradation is *silent* rather than breaking.

This is particularly relevant because this PR's core purpose is enabling passkeys during re-auth, and the password page is the primary re-auth surface. The `base` theme is the fallback for all custom themes that don't override individual templates.
findings.dimension_name: Theme macro renders hidden credentialId inputs; custom themes without the import silently degrade
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` (line 115-117) calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` which sets `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI=true` (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java line 43) and fills WebAuthn model data.
Step 2: `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge()` (line 127-133) calls `forms.createLoginUsernamePassword()` which renders `login-password.ftl` (Templates.java line 34: `case LOGIN_PASSWORD: return "login-password.ftl"`).
Step 3: `base/login/login-password.ftl` (52 lines) does NOT contain `<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>` or `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />`. The WebAuthn model data set in Step 1 is never consumed.
Step 4: Compare: `keycloak.v2/login/login-password.ftl` line 4: `<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>` and line 18: `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` — renders the hidden `credentialId`/`signature`/`authenticatorData`/`clientDataJSON`/`userHandle` inputs and passkey button.
Step 5: Compare: `base/login/login.ftl` line 2: `<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>`, line 83: `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` and `base/login/login-username.ftl` line 2: `<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>`, line 60: `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` — both base theme siblings DO call the macro, confirming this is an inconsistency/omission in base/login-password.ftl specifically.
Step 6: `passkeys.ftl` line 2: `<#if enableWebAuthnConditionalUI?has_content>` guards the entire macro body — safe no-op when flag not set.
Result: Custom themes extending `base` without overriding `login-password.ftl` silently lose passkey UI on the password page during re-auth.
findings.suggestion:
Add the passkeys import and macro call to `base/login/login-password.ftl` to match `base/login/login.ftl` and `base/login/login-username.ftl`:

```ftl
<#import "template.ftl" as layout>
<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>
<@layout.registrationLayout displayMessage=!messagesPerField.existsError('password'); section>
    ...
    <#elseif section = "form">
        ...
        <@passkeys.conditionalUIData />
    </#if>
</@layout.registrationLayout>
```

The macro already guards itself with `<#if enableWebAuthnConditionalUI?has_content>`, so it's a no-op when passkeys aren't enabled — safe to add unconditionally. This ensures the base theme is consistent across all three login pages (login, login-username, login-password) and custom themes inheriting from base get passkey support on the password page automatically.
findings.title: base/login/login-password.ftl missing passkeys.conditionalUIData macro call — custom themes extending base silently lose passkey UI on password page during re-auth

findings.blocking_reason: Incomplete rollout of a new passkeys feature in one template is a feature-completeness gap, not a regression or a breakage of existing contracts.
findings.body: The PR updated `base/login/login-username.ftl` and `base/login/login.ftl` with the passkeys macro but forgot `base/login/login-password.ftl`. Custom themes extending `base` directly will silently lose passkey support on the password step during re-auth with the split `PasswordForm` flow.
findings.title: base-theme-login-password-ftl-missing-passkeys-macro

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a semantic contract drift in a non-default SPI path with no demonstrated concrete production impact (no crash, data loss, security vulnerability, or broken default flow); the suggested fix is documentation and tests, which are non-blocking.
findings.body:
The PR adds `|| (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user))` to `PasswordForm.configuredFor`. The documented SPI contract of `Authenticator.configuredFor` (per `docs/documentation/server_development/topics/auth-spi.adoc` line 499-500) is: *"This method is responsible for determining if the user is configured for this particular authenticator."* For `PasswordForm`, that credential is the password. After this change, the method returns `true` for a user who has **no password** configured at all, as long as they have a WebAuthn passkey credential (or `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` is true realm-wide and the user has any WebAuthn credential).

This is a semantic broadening from *"is the user configured for the password authenticator"* to *"is the user able to authenticate through this form's UI (which may now render passkey UI)"*. The shift has real consequences for two secondary consumers of `configuredFor`:

1. **`ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator.matchCondition`** (`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/conditional/ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator.java:61`) — documented in `auth-spi.adoc:128-130` as evaluating `configuredFor` for sibling authenticators in a conditional subflow to decide whether the subflow acts as required or disabled. For a custom flow that places `Condition - User Configured` around a subflow containing `auth-password-form`, a passkey-only user previously caused `matchCondition` to return `false` (subflow disabled); now it returns `true` (subflow enabled). This flips flow branching for passkey-only users in any realm using the split username/password form with a `Condition - User Configured` gate.

2. **`AuthenticatorConfiguredMethod`** (`services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/AuthenticatorConfiguredMethod.java:46`) — exposes `configuredFor` to FreeMarker templates via `authenticatorConfiguredMethod.apply("auth-password-form")`. Custom themes that query this to decide which credential hints/UI to render now get `true` for passkey-only users. (Base themes do not currently use this method — confirmed via grep of `themes/**/*.ftl` — but the SPI surface is available to custom themes.)

The primary consumer (`DefaultAuthenticationFlow.java:445`) is the intended beneficiary: passkey-only users no longer hit `CREDENTIAL_SETUP_REQUIRED` (and since `PasswordFormFactory.isUserSetupAllowed()` returns `false`, that exception was not recoverable). That part is the desired behavior of the PR. The concern is the **undocumented contract drift** for the other two consumers, which were not updated and have no tests covering the passkey-only + conditional-flow scenario.

Note: the pre-existing `|| alreadyAuthenticatedUsingPasswordlessCredential(...)` term already stretched the contract, but that term is about *already-completed* authentication state (session-scoped), not about *user credential configuration*. The new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` term is a qualitatively different stretch: it reports the user as "configured for" an authenticator whose credential they do not possess.

This is a contract semantic shift, not a crash. The base browser flow uses `auth-username-password-form` (the combined `UsernamePasswordForm` whose `configuredFor` returns the hardcoded `true` with comment `// never called`), so default installations are unaffected. Only realms with a **split** flow using `auth-password-form` are impacted.
findings.dimension_name: PasswordForm.configuredFor semantics shift — now ORs in passkey-enabled, changing SPI contract
findings.evidence:
Step 1: PR changes `PasswordForm.configuredFor` (PasswordForm.java:61-65) to: `return user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(getCredentialProvider(session).getType()) || (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)) || alreadyAuthenticatedUsingPasswordlessCredential(session.getContext().getAuthenticationSession());`. Pre-PR version (git show 5af775db0f:...PasswordForm.java) was: `return user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(getCredentialProvider(session).getType()) || alreadyAuthenticatedUsingPasswordlessCredential(session.getContext().getAuthenticationSession());`.
Step 2: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-163) returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (currentUser == null || currentUser.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()))` — so for a user with a WebAuthn passkey credential but NO password credential, it returns true.
Step 3: `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator.isConfiguredFor` (line 61) calls `authenticator.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), context.getUser())` for each sibling non-conditional execution in the subflow. For a passkey-only user, this now returns `true` for `auth-password-form` where it previously returned `false`.
Step 4: Per `auth-spi.adoc:128-130`, `matchCondition` returns true if all required (or any alternative) siblings' `configuredFor` evaluate true. The flip from false→true for `auth-password-form` changes the conditional subflow from "disabled" to "enabled" for passkey-only users.
Step 5: `AuthenticatorConfiguredMethod.exec` (line 46) calls `authenticator.configuredFor(session, realm, user)` for an arbitrary providerId supplied by a FreeMarker template, so any custom theme querying `auth-password-form` now gets `true` for passkey-only users.
Step 6: `DefaultAuthenticationFlow.java:445` no longer throws `AuthenticationFlowError.CREDENTIAL_SETUP_REQUIRED` for passkey-only users (and `PasswordFormFactory.isUserSetupAllowed()` returns false, so the SETUP_REQUIRED branch was never taken) — this is the intended effect.
Step 7: No test in the PR covers `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator` + `auth-password-form` + passkey-only user; no test covers `AuthenticatorConfiguredMethod` for `auth-password-form`; the documented SPI contract (`auth-spi.adoc:499-500`) was not updated.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) document the contract broadening in the `Authenticator.configuredFor` javadoc and in `auth-spi.adoc`, explicitly stating that `PasswordForm.configuredFor` returns true when passkeys are available even without a password credential, and add a test covering `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator` + `auth-password-form` for a passkey-only user; or (b) keep `configuredFor` faithful to the credential-only semantics and instead handle the passkey-only case in `DefaultAuthenticationFlow` via a separate check (e.g., a new `isAlternativeCredentialAvailable` hook) so that `ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator` and `AuthenticatorConfiguredMethod` do not silently change behavior. Option (a) is lower-risk for back-compat with custom flows; option (b) is cleaner SPI-wise but requires flow-engine changes.
findings.title: PasswordForm.configuredFor broadens SPI semantics to OR-in passkey-enabled, changing contract for ConditionalUserConfiguredAuthenticator and theme method consumers

findings.blocking_reason: Removing final equals/hashCode/toString from JsonWebToken regresses all token subclasses from value-based equality to Object's identity-based equality, breaking the public org.keycloak.representations API contract with no migration path.
findings.body: The PR removes `final equals()`, `final hashCode()`, and `toString()` from JsonWebToken. Because these methods were declared `final`, ALL subclasses (IDToken, AccessToken, RefreshToken, LogoutToken, DPoP, PermissionTicketToken, AuthorizationResponseToken, DefaultActionTokenKey, TokenIntrospectionResponse, JwtCNonce, CIBAAuthenticationRequest, DockerResponseToken) were explicitly prohibited from overriding them and relied on the inherited value-based contract. After removal, every subclass silently inherits Object's identity-based equals/hashCode and the default `ClassName@hash` toString. This is a compound issue: the original cluster finding only flagged JsonWebToken itself, but the blast radius covers the entire token class hierarchy. The PR simultaneously modifies IDToken.java (31 lines), AccessToken.java (24 lines), RefreshToken.java (49 lines), and LogoutToken.java (6 lines) yet does NOT add replacement equals/hashCode/toString to any of them, confirming the cascade is unintended (or at least unmitigated). Consequences: (1) any downstream SPI/provider/custom protocol extension that places these token representations in HashMap, HashSet, or any value-based collection will silently switch from value-equality to identity-equality, causing lookup failures and duplicate entries; (2) any logging/debugging code that prints these tokens will lose the JSON-serialized toString output and instead see opaque `ClassName@hash` strings; (3) the `final` keyword was an explicit contract signal that value-based equality was the intended design — removing it without deprecation/migration breaks that contract for all consumers of the public `org.keycloak.representations` API. No in-repo breakage was found (no HashMap/HashSet of tokens, no token-to-token equals calls, no toString-in-logging), so the risk is primarily external/downstream rather than immediate.
findings.evidence: main branch JsonWebToken.java line 291 `public final boolean equals(Object o)` comparing id/exp/nbf/iat/issuer/audience/subject/type/issuedFor/otherClaims; line 310 hashCode using Objects.hashCode + Arrays.hashCode; toString serializing to JSON. pr-review branch JsonWebToken.java is 265 lines ending at getCategory() — all three methods removed. Subclasses verified to NOT define own equals/hashCode/toString on either branch: IDToken (line 28 `extends JsonWebToken`), AccessToken (line 37 `extends IDToken`), RefreshToken (line 30 `extends AccessToken`), LogoutToken (line 11 `extends JsonWebToken`). PR diff also touches AccessToken.java (24±), AccessTokenResponse.java (20±), IDToken.java (31±), LogoutToken.java (6±), RefreshToken.java (49±), UserInfo.java (37±). No `HashMap<Token>`/`HashSet<Token>`/`Map<Token>`/`Set<Token>` usage found in core; no token-to-token `.equals()` calls; no `log.debug(token)` toString usage; tests use `assertEquals(token.getFoo(), value)` on getters, not on token objects.
findings.suggestion: Either restore the final equals/hashCode/toString methods on JsonWebToken, OR explicitly add equals/hashCode/toString to each subclass that needs value-based semantics (IDToken, AccessToken, RefreshToken, LogoutToken, and any others used in collections or logging). If the removal is intentional (e.g., to allow subclasses to define their own), document the contract change and add replacement methods to subclasses in the same PR. At minimum, preserve toString() (or a JSON-serializing variant) on the parent to maintain debuggability across the token hierarchy. Consider a deprecation cycle rather than silent removal of a `final` contract.
findings.title: Removal of final equals()/hashCode()/toString() from JsonWebToken silently breaks API contract for ALL token subclasses (IDToken, AccessToken, RefreshToken, LogoutToken, etc.)

findings.body:
Scope: FreeMarker template import chain compiles/resolves at runtime for PR #41242/#41008 (passkeys re-auth flow).

Verified findings:
1. `<#import "passkeys.ftl">` resolves through parent chain: ExtendingTheme.getTemplate iterates child→parent; keycloak.v2 has parent=base; passkeys.ftl exists at base/login/
2. Established pattern in production: login-username.ftl (v2) already imports passkeys.ftl at line 5 — identical pattern
3. Macro signature matches call site: `<#macro conditionalUIData>` (no params) ↔ `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` (no args)
4. `authenticators` attribute name: WebAuthnConstants.ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS = "authenticators" matches FTL variable
5. Bean API matches FTL property access: getAuthenticators() → List<WebAuthnAuthenticatorBean>; getCredentialId() → String
6. All kc* properties defined: kcFormClass, kcButtonSecondaryClass, kcButtonBlockClass, kcMarginTopClass all in keycloak.v2 theme.properties

Conclusion: The new `<#import "passkeys.ftl" as passkeys>` at login-password.ftl:4 and `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData />` at line 18 will resolve correctly at runtime. The import follows an established pattern already present in login-username.ftl, the parent-theme fallback mechanism handles the missing file in keycloak.v2, and every variable/property/bean accessor used inside the macro body resolves against the data set by WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm. No blocking issues for this review dimension.
findings.title: Review Verdict: PASS - FreeMarker template import chain compiles/resolves at runtime

findings.blocking_reason: This is a maintainability/duplication concern with no current runtime bug or production impact; both copies are behaviorally identical today.
findings.body:
`AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` (lines 126–128) opens with the exact same sequence as `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (lines 257–259): read `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from the auth session via `getAuthNote(...)`, then parse it with `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)` to decide whether re-auth mode is active.

The two bodies are behaviorally identical today, but they are textually independent copies. The `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` **constant** is shared via `static import` (AuthenticatorUtils.java:35), so the auth-note *key* won't drift. However, the **parsing logic** (`getAuthNote` + `Boolean.parseBoolean`) is duplicated, and any future change to that logic — e.g., handling `null`/empty explicitly, switching to a tri-state, validating the stored value, or logging when the note is missing — must be applied in two unrelated files. The duplication exists because `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` is `protected` on `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` (package `...browser`) and `AuthenticatorUtils` lives in package `...util`, so the util class cannot call the protected method directly and re-implements it instead.

There are now three call sites that depend on this same predicate: `validateUserAndPassword` (line 129), `getUser` (line 139), `getDefaultChallengeMessage` (line 250) via the `protected` method, plus `badPasswordHandler` (line 222) and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` (line 53) via the util copy. A silent drift between the two implementations would cause the error-path form setup (USERNAME_HIDDEN, REGISTRATION_DISABLED) to disagree with the control-flow decisions (which user to load, which error message to show), producing inconsistent re-auth UI state.

This is a maintainability/drift concern, not a current runtime bug — both copies are equivalent at present.
findings.evidence:
Step 1: `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` (AuthenticatorUtils.java:126-128) executes: `String userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth = context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH);` followed by `if (Boolean.parseBoolean(userAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth)) { ... }`.
Step 2: `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-259) executes: `String userSet = context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH);` followed by `return Boolean.parseBoolean(userSet);`.
Step 3: The two sequences are textually identical (same auth-note key, same `Boolean.parseBoolean` parsing). The key constant is shared (AuthenticatorUtils.java:35 `import static ...AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH`), but the parsing is duplicated because `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` is `protected` (line 257) and `AuthenticatorUtils` is in a different package (`...util` vs `...browser`), so it cannot invoke the protected method.
Step 4: Result: two independent copies of the same predicate. Any future change to parsing semantics (null handling, value validation, logging) must be applied in both files or the error-path form setup will drift from the control-flow decisions in `validateUserAndPassword` (line 129), `getUser` (line 139), and `getDefaultChallengeMessage` (line 250), all of which use the `protected` copy while `badPasswordHandler` (line 222) and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` (line 53) use the util copy.
findings.suggestion:
Extract the predicate into a single `public static` method and have both call sites use it. Two options:

1. Move the helper into `AuthenticatorUtils` (already `public final`) as `public static boolean isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(AuthenticationFlowContext)` and have `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` delegate to it (or call the util version directly at lines 129, 139, 250). The constant is already accessible via static import.
2. Alternatively, widen `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` to `public static` and have `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` call it, removing the duplicated `getAuthNote` + `Boolean.parseBoolean` lines.

Either way, `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` becomes `if (isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)) { ... set USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED ... }`, leaving exactly one owner of the auth-note parsing.
findings.title: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError duplicates isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth's auth-note parsing logic

findings.blocking_reason: The finding describes a positive refactor and only speculates about potential API/serialization changes without concretely demonstrating broken callers or a regression.
findings.body: The `address` claim in `IDToken` was changed from being stored in the generic `otherClaims` map to a proper `@JsonProperty(ADDRESS)` field. This is a positive change: it improves type safety, makes the claim discoverable via IDE autocomplete, and ensures consistent serialization. However, the old `getAddressClaimsMap()` and `setAddress(Map)` methods were removed, so callers must use the new typed accessor. The serialization behavior may also change slightly (field ordering, null handling).
findings.title: IDToken.address promoted from otherClaims map to proper @JsonProperty field

findings.body: A new `ECCurve` enum (P256, P384, P521) was added with a `fromStdCrv(String)` factory method that maps standard curve names (P-256, secp256r1, prime256v1, P-384, secp384r1, P-521, secp521r1) to enum values. This is a positive addition that replaces ad-hoc string comparisons with type-safe enum values, reducing the risk of typo-related bugs in EC curve handling.
findings.title: New ECCurve enum with fromStdCrv() factory method — positive addition
